title: Weight and fall of a body with its own mark in the field of a held source

key_results.statement: Held body ($\tau=0$), couplings (a) and (c), $N_f\ge1$, $L\ge5$, every level and branch, lowest adapted field state, $|g_b|+|g_s|<t_f\omega_{\min}/2$: exactly $W_{k,\sigma}(x)-W_{k,\sigma}(x')=N_f[\varepsilon_0(x)-\varepsilon_0(x')]$, with $\varepsilon_0(x)$ the lowest eigenvalue of $h_x=C_1+g_bP_x+g_sP_{x_s}$, $g_b=\sigma\gamma M_k$.

Same class, first order in $g_s$, through second order in $\gamma$: $W_{k,\sigma}(x)=\mathrm{const}-\frac{2ng_sg_b}{t_f}\Lambda^+(x,x_s)+\frac{ng_sg_b^2}{t_f^2}[2G_0\Lambda^+(x,x_s)+\Lambda^+(x,x_s)^2-\frac2L(\Lambda^{+2})(x,x_s)]+O(g_s^2)+O(g_sg_b^3)$ at fixed $L,N_f,t_f$.
Same class and order, on the ring with $u=r(L-r)$: $W_{k,\sigma}(x)-W_{k,\sigma}(x')=\frac{ng_sg_b}{Lt_f}[(1-\frac{(L^2-2)g_b}{6Lt_f})(u-u')+\frac{g_b}{3Lt_f}(u^2-u'^2)]$, $g_b=\sigma\gamma M_k$.

Same class and order: the weight is $\sigma M_k\gamma\,\delta N(x)+M_k^2\gamma^2\Theta(x)$; at first order in $\gamma$ it is the one function $\gamma\delta N(x)$ of (5.8) times the factor $\sigma M_k$ (rest-and-clock cost) for all levels and both branches; through second order, for $\gamma g_s\ne0$, it does not factorize: its place dependence changes at relative order $\gamma$ between the two branches of every level and between levels with different $M_k$; no member of the class is a control.

Under regime R (R1: band of level $k$, branch $\sigma$ isolated, $\delta_{k,\sigma}>0$, $N_f(|\gamma|(M_k+\tau)+|g_s|)<\delta_{k,\sigma}/2$; start in the band with a real envelope $\phi$ on an arc of at most $L-4$ places not containing $x_s$; R2: coefficient of $\tau^2$), both couplings, first order in $g_s$: the drift acceleration from rest at $P=0$ is $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=-E''_{k,\sigma}(0)\sum_j\phi_{j+1}\phi_{j-1}W'_{k,\sigma}(j)+O(g_s^2)+O(\tau^4\gamma g_s)$, central slope.

Under R, both couplings, every start of the class (envelope nonnegative, symmetric about $x_0\ne x_s$, $c_\phi>0$; nonempty for $L\ge7$), first order in $g_s$, coefficient of $\tau^2$, through relative order $\gamma$: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=-\frac{\tau^2\gamma ng_s(L-2r_0)}{Lt_f}c_\phi[1+\epsilon\gamma n-\sigma\frac{\gamma M_k}{t_f}\frac{(L-2r_0)^2+2+12s_\phi^2}{6L}]+O(\tau^2g_s\gamma^3)+O(g_s^2)+O(\tau^4\gamma g_s)$, $\epsilon=-1$ (a), $+1$ (c), $c_\phi=\langle\cos2\hat P\rangle\in(0,1]$; meaningful for $\tau\ll M_k$ and $\tau^2\ll M_k\delta_{k,\sigma}$.

Same conditions: the fall is level- and branch-independent at leading order, $-\tau^2\gamma c_\phi\delta N'(x_0)$ for a common envelope, but not at relative order $\gamma$: the term $\Delta_{k,\sigma}=-\sigma\frac{\gamma M_k}{t_f}\frac{(L-2r_0)^2+2+12s_\phi^2}{6L}$, first order in $\gamma M_k/t_f$, odd in $\sigma$, proportional to $M_k$, geometric factor start-dependent and $\ge1/(3L)$, present for $\gamma g_s\ne0$ for every member and every start of the class with $L\ne2r_0$ (at the antipode $a=0$).

definitions.name: One-object contract with body and source point terms
Coupling of the body on level k and branch sigma to the field

Isolation gap of the band of level k and branch sigma

open_issues: Regime R is an assumption; the order τ⁴ of the acceleration (moving cloud, admixture of the other branch) is not computed.
The isolation and smallness conditions of R1 are sufficient conditions (norm bounds), not necessary ones.
(7.8) is derived for envelopes symmetric about a place; for other real envelopes (7.7) still holds, and the centre and third moment of the weights φ_{j+1}φ_{j−1} enter.
Field states other than the lowest adapted one, and the second order in g_s, are not treated (scope).

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of (7.8): τ, t_f, g_s, M_k in contract units, γ and n pure numbers; acceleration in position labels per λ² as in (5.7)
Test-body limit: dropping the own-mark term of (7.8) reproduces (5.7) with (5.8) through relative order γ for both couplings, up to the common momentum-width factor c_φ
Limits: (7.8) vanishes for τ→0 (flat dressed level, (6.7)), for g_s=0 (translation invariance) and at the antipode (reflection symmetry)
